items.title: FBI agent accused of stealing ~$1M in seized crypto
points: Court records allege an FBI agent misappropriated roughly $1 million in cryptocurrency (digital money recorded on a blockchain, a shared public ledger) that had been seized from an adversarial foreign nation.
The agent allegedly took the assets before voluntarily turning themselves in to authorities, which could mitigate legal consequences.
The case spotlights weak internal controls and oversight over how federal agencies custody and track confiscated digital assets.

items.title: BlackRock tokenizes $311B of European money market funds on Ethereum
points: BlackRock tokenized $311 billion of European money market funds — Europe's largest cash management platform — issuing tokens on Ethereum via JPMorgan's Kinexys platform.
Tokenization means converting traditional financial assets into digital tokens (blockchain-based ownership records) that can be traded and settled faster and around the clock.
Access is limited to professional investors across 13 European markets.
Follows Monday's launch of tokenized funds on Solana, Ethereum, and Stripe's Tempo blockchain for stablecoin reserves (stablecoins are crypto tokens pegged 1:1 to a currency like the US dollar).
CEO Larry Fink and COO Rob Goldstein call tokenization "the next major evolution in market infrastructure"; BlackRock's BUIDL tokenized money market fund now holds over $2.6 billion in assets.

items.title: Hardware wallet phishing wave: Coldcard losses near $130M
points: Phishing emails (fake messages impersonating a trusted company) posing as "coordinated hardware audits" send Coldcard users to cloned websites that install remote-access software.
Reported losses from the campaign are approaching $130 million.
Hardware wallet firms (devices that store crypto keys offline) are warning of a coordinated surge exploiting trust in official-looking security notices.

items.title: Hashdex to shut down its U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF
points: Brazil-based crypto asset manager Hashdex will liquidate its U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF (an exchange-traded fund holding actual Bitcoin) later this month after failing to attract enough assets.
It was one of the earliest U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, signaling consolidation in a crowded field.
